hero.headline: House passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding
hero.teaser: The House approved $70 billion in immigration enforcement funding that covers the remainder of President Trump's term.
hero.body:
The House passed legislation providing $70 billion for immigration enforcement through the end of President Trump's term. The bill now heads to the president's desk for his signature.

The legislation ends a four-month lapse in funding for immigration enforcement operations. The measure provides resources for border security and immigration enforcement activities under federal jurisdiction.

cards.headline: US Launches Strikes on Iran After Helicopter Downed Over Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States launched military strikes against Iran on Tuesday after a US Army Apache helicopter went down near the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump blamed Iranian forces for downing the aircraft and said the country "must, of necessity, respond to this attack."

US Central Command confirmed that strikes began at 10pm UK time, targeting radar and air defense facilities along the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes mark a significant escalation that endangers a ceasefire agreement announced by the two countries in April.

The helicopter crashed at approximately 3:30am local time off the coast of Oman during a patrol operation. A US official told the Associated Press that the helicopter collided with an Iranian drone, though it remained unclear whether the collision was intentional. Trump initially stated the helicopter had been "shot down," though official statements said the incident was under investigation.

Both crew members were rescued in an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat. The vessel, a 24-foot craft called a Corsair, located the aviators after they spent about two hours in the water. US Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins called it the first known drone rescue at sea by the US military.

However, Trump later downplayed the incident in an interview with the Wall Street Journal, calling it "wasn't a big deal" and noting that "the pilot is fine."

Central Command described the military response as "a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression," signaling that officials were not seeking a return to full-scale war. The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical waterway for global energy supplies, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the narrow passage between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.

The helicopter incident occurred as the region remained unstable following an exchange of fire between Iran and Israel on Monday, which further strained the ceasefire. Iranian state television reported that Israeli attacks killed at least two members of the country's air defense units.

The conflict that began on February 28 has shaken the global economy, raised energy prices worldwide, and made basic goods including food more expensive. Officials have struggled to convert the April ceasefire into a permanent agreement, particularly as Israel intensifies military operations in Lebanon against the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militia.

Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi responded to the strikes on social media, saying Iran "will leave no attack or threat unanswered. Leave our region if you want to be safe." Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated: "We prefer the language of diplomacy, but we speak other languages far more fluently."

Hours before the strikes, Trump had expressed renewed optimism about negotiations, saying there was "a good chance" of reaching a deal within "two or three days."

cards.headline: Dozens Feared Trapped After Strongest Earthquake in 50 Years Hits Philippines
cards.teaser: Families search for loved ones under rubble following the most powerful earthquake to strike the Philippines in half a century.
cards.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 37 people and injuring hundreds. The quake hit about 20 kilometers off the coast of Sarangani province, with powerful tremors felt across Mindanao and as far away as Manado in Indonesia.

Buildings collapsed across the region, and authorities warned people not to enter damaged structures due to risks from aftershocks. Rescue crews worked to reach those trapped in the rubble as families gathered at affected sites hoping to locate loved ones.

cards.headline: Social Security retirement trust fund projected to run dry in 2032
cards.teaser: The Social Security retirement trust fund will be depleted by 2032 unless Congress takes action, one year earlier than previously forecast.
cards.body:
Social Security's trust fund is expected to deplete its reserves in 2032 unless Congress takes action. The program's trustees warn the shortfall is accelerating, giving lawmakers less than seven years to address the issue.

Once depleted, Social Security would only be able to pay benefits from incoming payroll taxes. This would force automatic reductions in benefits for retirees. Demographic shifts, including longer lifespans and declining birth rates, have strained the system by reducing the ratio of workers supporting each beneficiary.

cards.headline: UK and Allies Impose Sanctions Over Settler Violence in West Bank
cards.teaser: Britain and partner nations announced sanctions targeting networks that enable settler violence in the occupied West Bank.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom and allied nations, including Australia, have imposed sanctions targeting networks they say facilitate settler violence in the West Bank. France announced it would ban far-right Israeli Minister Bezalel Smotrich from entering the country as part of the coordinated action.

Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong issued a statement highlighting "horrific levels of settler violence against Palestinian civilians" as the reason for the joint action with Western allies. Israel has condemned the sanctions as "disgraceful."

cards.headline: Myanmar Military Gains Ground as Rebels Face Forced Conscription
cards.teaser: Government forces in Myanmar are pushing men into military service as rebel groups lose territory in the ongoing civil war.
cards.body:
Myanmar's military has gained ground against rebel forces while implementing forced conscription to bolster its ranks. The civil war, which began after the military seized power in 2021, has displaced millions and created a humanitarian crisis.

The BBC traveled with rebel fighters to frontline positions to document how the conflict is developing. Reporters documented the rebels' positions as the military continues its advance across the country.

cards.headline: House passes bill allowing government intervention in union contract negotiations
cards.body:
The House approved legislation designed to accelerate contract negotiations for newly unionized workers, with 20 Republicans breaking ranks to support the Democratic-led measure. The bill would allow government intervention if employers and unions fail to reach an agreement within 90 days of workers voting to unionize.

Speaker Mike Johnson opposed the measure and urged House Republicans to vote against it, but the defections provided enough support to pass the bill. The vote demonstrates a continuing pattern of House Republicans bypassing their own leadership to back Democratic legislation.

Under existing law, newly unionized workers often wait months or years to secure their first contract as employers and unions negotiate terms. The legislation aims to shorten this timeline by establishing a 90-day deadline. If negotiations stall beyond that point, federal mediators can intervene to help resolve disputes.

Supporters of the bill argue it will prevent employers from deliberately prolonging negotiations as a tactic to discourage union organizing. Union leaders have long maintained that extended delays in securing first contracts undermine organizing efforts and leave workers without promised benefits they voted to obtain.

The 20 Republicans who voted for the measure represent a significant departure from traditional party opposition to pro-union legislation. Their support reflects growing labor activism in their districts and pressure from constituents who have recently organized their workplaces. The bill now advances to the Senate, where its prospects remain uncertain given the chamber's political composition.

The House vote provides a victory for labor organizations that have pushed for stronger protections for newly unionized workers. The passage comes during a period of increased union organizing across multiple industries, including retail, technology, and hospitality sectors.

This outcome continues a recent trend where House Republicans have crossed party lines to support Democratic priorities despite leadership opposition. With the chamber narrowly divided and Republicans holding a slim majority, defections from either party can significantly impact legislative outcomes. The ability of Democrats to secure Republican votes on labor issues suggests potential vulnerability within the GOP caucus on issues where constituents have expressed strong interest in union protection.

Union leaders view the bill as an important step toward protecting workers' right to organize and bargain collectively. They argue that without mechanisms to accelerate contract negotiations, employers can use delay tactics to discourage future unionization efforts, effectively undermining the organizing victories workers have already achieved through their votes.

The bill's journey to the Senate will test whether the bipartisan support demonstrated in the House exists in the upper chamber, where procedural rules and a different political calculation may affect its prospects for passage.

cards.headline: Man Arrested After Stabbing Attack in Belfast Sparks Unrest
cards.teaser: A 30-year-old Sudanese man was charged following an assault in Belfast that was recorded and spread quickly online, triggering protests.
cards.body:
Police in Belfast arrested and charged a 30-year-old Sudanese man following a stabbing attack on another man. The assault was recorded and spread rapidly across social media platforms.

The incident triggered widespread unrest across Northern Ireland, with protesters setting fires to vehicles and homes. Roads were also blocked as demonstrations erupted in response to the attack.

cards.teaser: Britain and partner nations announced sanctions targeting networks that enable settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

cards.headline: Albania Faces EU Pressure Over Kushner Resort Project
cards.teaser: Brussels is pressing Albania over a luxury resort planned by Jared Kushner that threatens to violate European Union environmental law.
cards.body:
The European Union is urging Albania to address concerns about a luxury resort project planned by Jared Kushner, son-in-law of President Trump. The development on a protected beach threatens to conflict with EU environmental regulations as Albania seeks membership in the bloc.

Local residents and environmental groups have protested the resort plans, which they say would damage protected coastal areas. The project has become a test case for Albania's commitment to EU standards as it pursues accession to the union.

cards.headline: Somali Referee Denied US Entry, Missing World Cup Opportunity
cards.teaser: Omar Abdulkadir Artan says his dream of becoming the first Somali to referee a World Cup match ended when the United States turned him away.
cards.body:
Omar Abdulkadir Artan, a Somali referee, was denied entry to the United States despite possessing proper documentation, preventing him from officiating at the World Cup. In his first interview since being turned back, Artan stated he had all necessary papers and required materials for entry.

Had he been allowed to compete, Artan would have made history as the first Somali national to referee a World Cup match. He described the opportunity as a dream chance to represent his country on the global stage.

cards.headline: House approves $70 billion for immigration enforcement through 2027
cards.teaser: House Republicans passed a three-year funding bill for border and immigration operations, sending it to President Trump.
cards.body:
The House passed a $70 billion bill to fund immigration enforcement agencies through the remainder of President Trump's term. The legislation allocates resources for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol operations over three years.

Republicans supported the measure while Democrats opposed it, warning that Congress has ceded its oversight role. The bill now goes to President Trump for his signature, reflecting GOP support for the administration's immigration agenda.

cards.headline: Republican Steve Hilton advances to California governor general election
cards.teaser: Steve Hilton secured the second spot in California's gubernatorial race and will face Democrat Xavier Becerra in November.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality, has advanced to the November general election for California governor. He will face Democrat Xavier Becerra, a former congressman, state attorney general and US health secretary. 

Hilton's advancement came after receiving an endorsement from Donald Trump. California's top-two primary system allows the two highest vote-getters to proceed to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: White House restricts press access to UFC event, ceding credential control to promotion
cards.teaser: The White House will close its grounds to reporters during an upcoming UFC fight unless the sports organization grants them access.
cards.body:
The White House will be closed to reporters during an upcoming UFC fight on its grounds unless the promotion provides press credentials. This arrangement gives UFC officials control over which journalists can cover the event, departing from standard White House press access protocols.

Extensive road closures are planned around Washington for the event. A super PAC supporting President Trump is hosting a fundraiser the day before the fight with tickets priced at $1 million per person.

cards.headline: Democrat Mai Vang advances to face incumbent Doris Matsui in California House race
cards.teaser: Sacramento Councilmember Mai Vang will challenge longtime Representative Doris Matsui in November after leading the primary.
cards.body:
Sacramento Councilmember Mai Vang advanced to the November general election for California's 7th Congressional District, where she will face incumbent Democrat Doris Matsui. Vang led the primary vote count in the Sacramento-area district.

The race represents a generational challenge to Matsui, who has held the seat for multiple terms. Both candidates are Democrats, meaning the general election will be an intraparty contest. Vang's advancement sets up a November race focusing on age and experience versus new leadership in the heavily Democratic district.

cards.headline: Maine holds primaries for Senate and governor races
cards.teaser: Graham Platner seeks the Democratic nomination for Senate as Maine voters choose candidates in several statewide races.
cards.body:
Maine voters cast ballots in primary elections for Senate and governor. Graham Platner secured the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate, with author Stephen King announcing his support for the candidate on social media.

Platner's main competitor, Maine Governor Janet Mills, had suspended her campaign due to lack of funds. However, some out-of-state Democrats launched a late push for Mills after Platner faced accusations from a former romantic partner of physical abuse.

cards.headline: NHS to offer five-session radiotherapy treatment for prostate cancer
cards.teaser: Men in England with prostate cancer will be offered an advanced treatment that reduces sessions from 20 to five.
cards.body:
Some men in England with prostate cancer will now receive an advanced form of radiotherapy on the National Health Service that requires only five treatment sessions instead of 20. The new approach represents a significant reduction in the time patients must spend receiving treatment.

The advanced radiotherapy delivers higher doses of radiation in fewer sessions while maintaining treatment effectiveness. The change aims to reduce the burden on patients who previously needed to attend multiple appointments over several weeks. The treatment is being rolled out as part of NHS efforts to modernize cancer care.

hero.headline: Apollo and Blackstone raise $35 billion to finance AI chip infrastructure for Anthropic
hero.body:
Apollo Global Management and Blackstone have raised $35 billion in a new financing arrangement with chipmaker Broadcom to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure for Anthropic, the AI startup backed by Google. The deal represents one of the largest private financing packages assembled for AI hardware deployment.

Broadcom will help structure and manage chip supply arrangements under the financing platform, which is designed to support Anthropic's expansion of computing capacity. Google has provided financial guarantees underpinning portions of the agreement, according to reports. The arrangement allows Anthropic to scale its AI operations without committing the full capital upfront for expensive semiconductor orders and data center infrastructure.

The financing structure addresses a growing challenge in the AI industry: the massive upfront costs required to secure advanced chips and build the computing infrastructure needed to train and run large language models. Companies like Anthropic and OpenAI require billions of dollars in specialized hardware, primarily graphics processing units and custom AI accelerators, to remain competitive. Traditional venture capital and corporate funding often prove insufficient for these capital requirements.

Apollo and Blackstone, two of the world's largest alternative asset managers, have increasingly moved into technology infrastructure investments as AI development accelerates. The firms see opportunities to provide capital for physical assets like chips and servers that have predictable demand from well-funded AI companies. Broadcom, which designs custom chips for major technology companies, gains a financing mechanism that can help its AI customers afford larger orders.

The arrangement comes as competition intensifies among AI labs to secure computing resources. Access to cutting-edge chips has become a strategic bottleneck, with manufacturing capacity constrained and prices elevated. By securing committed financing, Anthropic aims to lock in supply and expand its infrastructure as it competes with rivals including OpenAI and technology giants developing their own AI systems. The deal also reflects growing confidence among financial institutions that AI infrastructure represents a sound investment as the technology moves from research to commercial deployment across industries.

cards.headline: Social Security retirement trust fund projected to run dry in 2032
cards.teaser: The Social Security retirement trust fund will be depleted by 2032 unless Congress takes action, one year earlier than previously forecast.
cards.body:
Social Security's trust fund is expected to deplete its reserves in 2032 unless Congress takes action. The program's trustees warn the shortfall is accelerating, giving lawmakers less than seven years to address the issue.

cards.headline: SpaceX initial public offering nearly four times oversubscribed
cards.teaser: Demand for shares in SpaceX's public offering is approaching four times the available allocation, according to a source familiar with the matter.
cards.body:
The initial public offering of SpaceX has drawn demand approaching four times the number of shares available, indicating strong investor appetite for the space exploration company founded by Elon Musk. The level of oversubscription suggests institutional and retail investors are competing heavily for allocation in the offering.

SpaceX has built a dominant position in commercial space launches and operates the Starlink satellite internet service, which has grown to serve millions of subscribers globally. The company's valuation and the specific timing of the offering have generated significant attention on Wall Street, though some pension fund managers have criticized what they describe as governance practices that disadvantage outside shareholders.

cards.headline: General Motors to develop sodium-ion batteries for energy storage
cards.teaser: General Motors plans to produce sodium-ion battery cells for stationary energy storage systems rather than electric vehicles as EV sales growth slows.
cards.body:
General Motors is developing sodium-ion battery technology for energy storage applications, partnering with Peak Energy to scale the technology. Unlike lithium-ion batteries used in vehicles, sodium-ion cells rely on more abundant and affordable materials, making them cost-effective for stationary energy storage in data centers, factories, and other industrial applications.

The move positions GM to compete in the growing energy storage market alongside Tesla, which already supplies large-scale battery systems to utilities and commercial customers. Sodium-ion batteries are designed to help balance power supply and demand on electrical grids without requiring the high energy density needed for vehicle propulsion.

cards.headline: TSMC warns of possible price increases as production costs rise
cards.teaser: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company has not ruled out raising prices as the world's largest chipmaker faces increasing production costs.
cards.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's senior leadership has indicated the firm may raise prices as it contends with mounting production expenses. In a rare interview, the executive addressed how the company is managing surging demand from artificial intelligence while handling the geopolitical challenges of manufacturing most of the world's advanced chips in Taiwan.

Any price increases from TSMC would likely affect consumers through higher costs for electronics and computers. The company produces cutting-edge semiconductors for major clients including Apple, Nvidia, and AMD.

cards.headline: Kalshi introduces employment verification to combat insider trading
cards.teaser: Prediction betting platform Kalshi will require some users to disclose employer information and launches whistleblower services after facing insider trading concerns.
cards.body:
Kalshi is implementing employment verification requirements for users trading in certain markets as part of new compliance measures against insider trading. The prediction market platform will require customers to disclose employer information when placing bets in high-risk categories vulnerable to insider knowledge, such as economic data releases and regulatory decisions.

The initiative also includes establishing whistleblower services. These changes follow scrutiny over potential insider trading activity on the platform, where individuals with advance knowledge could unfairly profit from bets on outcomes like Federal Reserve decisions or congressional actions. The employment disclosure requirement aims to identify conflicts of interest and flag suspicious trading patterns.

cards.headline: Most consumers unaware of special tariffs for water and broadband bills
cards.teaser: The majority of bill payers do not know about discounted tariffs available for water and broadband services, according to a spending watchdog.
cards.body:
Most people paying for water and broadband services are unaware that special discounted tariffs exist for eligible customers, a spending watchdog has found. The finding suggests millions of households may be paying standard rates when they qualify for reduced bills.

Utility companies and internet service providers offer social tariffs designed to make essential services more affordable for low-income households, but awareness and take-up remain low. The watchdog's report indicates that better outreach and simpler application processes could help more eligible consumers access the discounts, reducing the burden of essential service costs on household budgets.

hero.headline: NASA names four astronauts for Artemis III lunar mission training
hero.body:
NASA announced the crew for its Artemis III mission on Tuesday, revealing the next phase of the agency's efforts to return humans to the Moon. The space agency selected four astronauts who will launch in 2027 for a two-week test flight in low Earth orbit, paving the way for a planned crewed lunar landing in 2028.

The crew includes Randy Bresnik of NASA as mission commander, Luca Parmitano of the European Space Agency as pilot, and NASA mission specialists Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas. NASA also named Bob Hines as a support crew member. Bresnik is a Marine colonel and former commander of the International Space Station with more than 7,000 hours of flying time. Parmitano is a fighter pilot in the Italian air force who previously experienced a near-fatal incident during a 2013 spacewalk when his helmet filled with liquid. Rubio, an Army Black Hawk helicopter pilot and flight surgeon, holds the record for the longest single spaceflight duration by a NASA astronaut at 371 days. Douglas, a systems engineer and Coast Guard reserve officer, has no previous spaceflight experience but trained as a backup crew member for Artemis II.

Unlike the Artemis II mission that looped around the Moon, the Artemis III crew will remain in low Earth orbit to test critical systems. They will practice docking procedures and evaluate life support systems for two competing lunar landers from Blue Origin and SpaceX ahead of the actual Moon landing.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman described the announcement as marking the creation of "Earth's first starfleet," emphasizing the international scope of the program. He highlighted the numerous spacecraft that will operate simultaneously, including vehicles from NASA, Russia, China, Blue Origin, and SpaceX.

The announcement also addressed recent setbacks facing the program. Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, designed to carry its lunar lander, was destroyed in a launchpad explosion on May 28. John Couluris, Blue Origin's senior vice-president of lunar permanence, acknowledged the incident but expressed confidence that the company would rebuild and meet the 2027 launch timeline.

Jeremy Parsons, NASA's acting deputy associate administrator for the Moon to Mars program, confirmed NASA's commitment to supporting its partners through technical challenges. "While we recognize there are questions about how Blue Origin's recent anomaly impacts our plans, setbacks are a learning opportunity," he said.

The Artemis program represents an expansion of lunar exploration through international collaboration. The selection of Parmitano marks the first time a European astronaut will participate in a NASA Artemis mission, demonstrating how multiple nations are contributing to humanity's return to the Moon more than 50 years after Apollo 17 in 1972.

cards.headline: Commonwealth Fusion Systems publishes design for 400-megawatt fusion reactor
cards.teaser: The company released five peer-reviewed papers detailing its planned commercial reactor and modeling its expected power output.
cards.body:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems made public the technical case for its planned fusion reactor, which the company projects will generate 400 megawatts of power. The design details appeared in five peer-reviewed papers that update the reactor's specifications and model its anticipated performance.

The papers represent an effort to document the physics and engineering behind the commercial reactor Commonwealth Fusion aims to build. Fusion energy has long been pursued as a potential clean power source, but no company or research institution has yet operated a fusion reactor that produces more energy than it consumes on a sustained, commercially viable basis.

cards.headline: General Motors develops sodium-ion batteries for data centers and grid storage
cards.teaser: The automaker is creating a new battery chemistry for use beyond vehicles, targeting AI infrastructure and industrial facilities.
cards.body:
General Motors is developing a new sodium-ion battery chemistry designed for stationary energy storage applications. The technology targets data centers, electrical grids, and GM's own manufacturing facilities, marking an expansion beyond the company's traditional focus on electric vehicle batteries.

Sodium-ion batteries use different materials than the lithium-ion cells currently dominant in EVs and consumer electronics. For stationary applications like grid storage, the weight disadvantages that make sodium-ion less suitable for vehicles become irrelevant, positioning the technology as a viable solution for large-scale energy storage needs.

cards.headline: Google cuts price of budget AI subscription tier
cards.teaser: The company reduced pricing for its lower-cost AI subscription offering.
cards.body:
Google lowered the cost of its budget-tier AI subscription service. The price reduction comes as multiple technology companies compete for paid subscribers to generative AI tools.

The move marks a shift in pricing strategy as companies test how much consumers will pay for AI features. Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and others have introduced subscription tiers over the past year, with prices varying based on usage limits and feature access.

cards.headline: Starlink adds monthly hardware fee and raises service prices
cards.teaser: SpaceX's satellite internet service now charges a $10 monthly fee for equipment and increased subscription costs by $5 to $10.
cards.body:
Starlink introduced a $10 monthly hardware fee for its satellite internet equipment, moving away from the one-time purchase model it previously used. The company also raised service subscription prices by $5 to $10 per month depending on the plan.

The changes affect customers of Starlink, which has become SpaceX's largest revenue source. The satellite internet service operates in dozens of countries, providing connectivity in rural and remote areas where traditional broadband infrastructure does not reach.

cards.headline: Microsoft patches two zero-day vulnerabilities disclosed by researcher
cards.teaser: The company fixed security flaws revealed by a researcher with whom Microsoft has had public disagreements.
cards.body:
Microsoft released patches for two zero-day vulnerabilities disclosed by the security researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse. The fixes address security flaws that could be exploited before patches were available.

The patches come amid an ongoing public dispute between Microsoft and the researcher. Zero-day vulnerabilities refer to security flaws that are exploited before the software maker has issued a fix, giving defenders zero days to prepare.

cards.headline: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 generates simple video games from text prompts
cards.teaser: The AI model can create playable games through conversational commands.
cards.body:
Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, its first Mythos-class model available to the public. The company describes it as the most powerful model it has made widely available, demonstrating exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks. The model's advantages over competitors grow as tasks become longer and more complex.

The tool allows users to create simple interactive games by describing what they want in natural language. Anthropic built guardrails into the model that block responses in high-risk areas like cybersecurity and biology, balancing capability with safety considerations.

hero.headline: Serena Williams wins doubles match in return to tennis after nearly four years
hero.body:
Serena Williams made a winning professional tennis comeback at age 44, partnering with Canadian teenager Victoria Mboko to defeat third seeds Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Erin Routliffe 7-6 (7-2), 6-2 in the first round of doubles at Queen's Club.

The victory marked Williams' return to competition after 1,375 days away from the sport. She had stepped back from professional tennis in 2022, having won 23 Grand Slam singles titles throughout her career.

The first set proved competitive, with the unseeded pair needing a tiebreak to secure the opening set. They controlled the tiebreak decisively before dominating the second set to claim the match in straight sets. The win came against seeded opponents, demonstrating that Williams retains the competitive skills that defined her legendary career.

Williams chose to return through doubles rather than singles, allowing her to ease back into competitive tennis with a partner. When assessing her performance after the match, she gave herself a modest grade, acknowledging room for improvement as she rebuilds her competitive fitness.

In discussing her comeback motivation, Williams emphasized that winning is no longer her primary concern. "I don't need to win. I've won more than most people have in their whole lives, so for me it's not important," she said. She explained that the return is largely about her children experiencing her as a competitor. She gave birth to a daughter in 2023 and has an eight-year-old daughter, Olympia.

Williams selected Mboko, the world number 9 in singles, as her partner after being impressed by the teenager's attitude and drive. "I remember seeing her play in Montreal. I was impressed with her attitude, and what I liked the most about her was that the next time she played she still kept winning," Williams said. She noted that Mboko "reminded me a lot of myself."

For Mboko, the partnership holds special significance. Growing up, Williams had been her idol. "It was really hard not to like her because she won every tournament she played," Mboko said. She added that meeting Williams in person revealed her to be "really nice and very personable, very relatable. And I think she's really funny."

Williams has committed to playing doubles in Berlin following Queen's but said her future in singles remains uncertain. When asked about returning to singles competition, she stated: "I can't say yeah, I can't say no. Right now, no." She suggested she would need additional training to compete in singles and emphasized that her current focus is on enjoying the experience.

The Queen's Club tournament serves as a grass-court warmup event before Wimbledon. Williams and Mboko will compete in the second round of the doubles draw.

cards.headline: Marco Silva agrees to become Benfica head coach as Jose Mourinho departs for Real Madrid
cards.teaser: Benfica formalized the departure of Jose Mourinho and reached an agreement with Marco Silva to become the club's new head coach.
cards.body:
Portuguese club Benfica has formalized Jose Mourinho's departure to Real Madrid and moved swiftly to secure his replacement. Marco Silva has agreed to become Benfica's new head coach, taking over the position left vacant by Mourinho's exit.

The managerial transition marks a significant change for the Portuguese club as it transitions leadership following Mourinho's move to the Spanish capital.

cards.headline: England beats Ukraine 3-0 but misses automatic World Cup qualification spot
cards.teaser: England defeated Ukraine 3-0 but failed to secure automatic qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup because the result was out of their hands.
cards.body:
England's women's national team defeated Ukraine 3-0 on Tuesday, but the result could not change their fate in World Cup qualification. The team finished second in their group and will compete in the playoffs for a spot at the 2027 Women's World Cup instead of securing automatic qualification.

Manager Sarina Wiegman acknowledged the disappointment, reflecting on Friday's match as a difficult one that failed to build momentum. England's path to the World Cup now depends on performing well in the playoff stage.

cards.headline: Hurricanes start Brandon Bussi in goal for Game 4 of Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: The Carolina Hurricanes will turn to goaltender Brandon Bussi for Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
Carolina Hurricanes head coach Rod Brind'Amour confirmed that Brandon Bussi will start in goal for Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final against the Vegas Golden Knights. Bussi replaces Pyotr Kochetkov, who has been moved to the backup role ahead of Frederik Andersen.

The goaltending change represents Bussi's debut in the Stanley Cup Final. The Hurricanes face a critical situation in Game 4, with the team needing to avoid falling further behind in the series. Brind'Amour's decision to start Bussi marks a significant shift in the team's approach to the championship round.

cards.headline: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez attends mandatory minicamp amid contract talks
cards.teaser: New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez reported to the team's mandatory minicamp and reaffirmed his commitment to the franchise.
cards.body:
Christian Gonzalez attended the first day of the New England Patriots' mandatory minicamp, ending speculation about his absence during earlier voluntary workouts. The cornerback has been engaged in contract discussions with the team but showed up for the required practice sessions.

Gonzalez stated his desire to remain with the Patriots organization despite ongoing negotiations. He was present and participated in the first minicamp practice alongside teammates, including wide receiver Kayshon Boutte. The attendance satisfied the mandatory requirement while contract talks continue between the player and the team.

cards.headline: England manager Thomas Tuchel managing Bukayo Saka's fitness ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: England head coach Thomas Tuchel said the team is exercising caution with forward Bukayo Saka's fitness as the World Cup approaches.
cards.body:
Thomas Tuchel has confirmed that Bukayo Saka is playing through an achilles injury as England prepares for the World Cup. The Arsenal winger received an extra week off following the Champions League final before joining up with the England squad in West Palm Beach, where his physical condition continues to be carefully monitored.

Tuchel acknowledged that Saka is not yet at full fitness, stating that "some things are missing" from his game. The manager is managing the forward's availability cautiously as the tournament approaches, balancing the need to have key players available while protecting them from further injury.

cards.headline: West Ham owner banned from contact with women's and youth teams since 2023
cards.teaser: West Ham United owner has been prohibited from contact with the club's women's and youth teams following a safeguarding investigation.
cards.body:
David Sullivan, West Ham's co-chair, has been barred from contact with the club's women's and youth teams following a safeguarding investigation by the Football Association. The restriction has been in place since 2023.

Sullivan stepped down from his position ahead of allegations about his private life, which he denies.

hero.headline: Nick Reiner Seeks Access to Trust Funds for Legal Defense in Parents' Murder Case
hero.body:
Nick Reiner entered a not guilty plea to two counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of his parents Rob and Michele Reiner during his arraignment in Los Angeles on Monday. Public defender Kimberly Greene represented Reiner, who stood in a custody area wearing jail clothes as the proceedings took place.

The 32-year-old has been held without bail since his arrest in December following the discovery of his parents' bodies in their Los Angeles home on December 14. Rob Reiner, 78, was an acclaimed director and actor, while Michele, 70, was a photographer. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner determined both died from multiple sharp force injuries.

Reiner's case involves first-degree murder charges with special circumstances for multiple murders and an allegation of using a dangerous weapon. The district attorney's office is still awaiting a complete autopsy report. Los Angeles District Attorney Nathan Hochman indicated that the case is eligible for the death penalty but that his office has not yet decided whether to pursue capital charges.

"We will be looking at all aggravating and mitigating circumstances," Hochman told reporters after the arraignment.

The change in legal representation marks the second attorney shift in the case. Reiner's former attorney, Alan Jackson, withdrew from the case last month without explaining his reasons, though he stated at the time that his client was not guilty. A judge had postponed proceedings following Jackson's withdrawal before Greene took over the case.

The killings sent shockwaves through the entertainment industry given the prominence of Rob and Michele Reiner, who were also known for their political activism. The case has received extensive media coverage, with reports detailing Reiner's personal struggles including a history of addiction and mental illness. He had been placed under a conservatorship for a year in 2020 due to mental health issues and was reportedly prescribed medication for schizophrenia prior to the killings.

According to media reports, Reiner's behavior had become increasingly erratic in the period leading up to the deaths. The night before their bodies were discovered, the couple attended a Christmas party at comedian Conan O'Brien's home where Rob and Nick Reiner were heard arguing. O'Brien later described the victims as "lovely people" and expressed his shock at losing friends he and his wife had grown close to.

Jackson had previously urged the public not to rush to judgment in the case, saying that circumstances beyond his control made continuing representation impossible.

Reiner is scheduled to next appear in court on April 29.

cards.headline: Jay-Z and Eminem Collaborate on New Rakim Album
cards.teaser: The two rappers reunite for their first track together in 25 years on a collaborative album featuring Rakim, Kurupt, and Masta Killa.
cards.body:
Jay-Z and Eminem will appear together on a new Rakim album, marking their first collaboration in 25 years. The track is part of a collaborative project that also features rappers Kurupt and Masta Killa.

The collaboration represents a reunion of major figures in hip-hop history. Both Jay-Z and Eminem pay homage to Rakim, who is widely regarded as one of the most influential rappers in the genre's history. The album brings together artists from different eras of hip-hop for the project.

cards.headline: Summer House Reunion Episodes Draw Record Viewership
cards.teaser: The first two parts of the Season 10 reunion attracted the largest audience in the reality show's history.
cards.body:
The first two parts of the Summer House Season 10 reunion have achieved a ratings milestone for the reality series. Part one drew the largest Live+Same Day audience in the show's history, according to NBCUniversal.

The reunion's strong performance extended across multiple platforms during its first week of availability, marking the show's best performance to date and demonstrating sustained viewer interest in the series.

cards.headline: Toy Story 5 Merchandise Campaign Expands Beyond Traditional Toys
cards.teaser: The upcoming Pixar film has inspired a wide-ranging merchandise lineup including luggage, jewelry, and collectibles ahead of its theatrical release.
cards.body:
Toy Story 5 has launched a comprehensive merchandise campaign featuring partnerships with Lego, Funko, Away Luggage, and Pandora Jewelry. The product lineup includes special-edition Uno cards, Funko Pop figures, and Lego sets, alongside collaborations with brands not traditionally tied to animated films.

The film's release next weekend marks a significant commercial push for the franchise. Tom Hanks has commented on the movie's central theme, noting that Woody, Buzz, and other toys compete with a tablet for children's attention, reflecting concerns about screen addiction.

cards.headline: FX Sets August Premiere for Adults Season 2
cards.teaser: The entire eight-episode second season will be released on August 27 with guest appearances from Jake Shane and Gaten Matarazzo.
cards.body:
FX has set August 27 as the premiere date for Adults Season 2. The complete eight-episode season drops simultaneously on FXX on-demand and Hulu at 9 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. PT that day.

The season will air weekly on the FXX linear channel while the full season becomes immediately available for streaming. Guest stars for the season include Jake Shane and Gaten Matarazzo. International viewers can access the series on Disney+.

cards.headline: Hacks Costume Designer Used Real Playing Cards for Jean Smart's Dress
cards.teaser: The Queen of Hearts costume required hand-stitching actual playing cards onto the garment for the show's final season.
cards.body:
Costume designer Kathleen Felix-Hager created a dress made from real playing cards for Jean Smart's character Deborah in Episode 3 of Hacks' final season. The designer drew inspiration from a single line in the script that mentioned Deborah appearing in a playing card dress.

Felix-Hager hand-stitched the playing cards onto the garment to complete the Queen of Hearts costume. She had time early in production to develop and execute the concept, working with the production team to finalize the piece's appearance.

cards.headline: Chris Brown Settles Copyright Lawsuit Over Songs
cards.teaser: The singer settled a lawsuit from a lyricist who accused him of denying credit and withholding revenue for tracks including Monalisa and Sensational.
cards.body: Chris Brown has settled a lawsuit filed by a lyricist over the songs Monalisa and Sensational. The plaintiff had accused Brown of denying proper credit for the work and cutting the lyricist out of millions of dollars in revenue. The lawsuit centered on allegations that Brown failed to provide appropriate songwriting credits and compensation for the plaintiff's contributions to the songs.

hero.headline: House passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding
hero.teaser: The House approved $70 billion in immigration enforcement funding that covers the remainder of President Trump's term.
hero.body:
The House passed legislation providing $70 billion for immigration enforcement through the end of President Trump's term. The bill now heads to the president's desk for his signature.

The legislation ends a four-month lapse in funding for immigration enforcement operations. The measure provides resources for border security and immigration enforcement activities under federal jurisdiction.

cards.headline: Trump appoints Pulte as acting intelligence chief earlier than planned
cards.teaser: President Trump announced Bill Pulte will assume the role of acting Director of National Intelligence sooner than originally scheduled.
cards.body:
President Trump announced on Tuesday that Bill Pulte will assume the role of acting Director of National Intelligence sooner than originally planned. The accelerated appointment comes as Trump met with House Speaker Mike Johnson at the White House to discuss the nomination.

The timing is significant because Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act—which allows US intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets overseas without a court warrant—expires at midnight Thursday. Some Republicans believe nominating a permanent intelligence director is necessary to secure reauthorization of the surveillance law before the deadline.

cards.headline: U.S. launches third round of strikes against Iranian air defenses
cards.teaser: The United States launched multiple rounds of military strikes against Iranian targets beginning at 5 p.m.
cards.body:
President Trump directed the U.S. military to launch strikes against Iran beginning at 5 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, following Iran's downing of a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. The helicopter's crew was rescued by drone. U.S. Central Command confirmed the strikes targeted Iranian radar and air defense facilities in the region.

A third round of strikes followed shortly after 8 p.m. Eastern Time. The military action jeopardizes a ceasefire announced between the U.S. and Iran in April and raises concerns about broader escalation in the Middle East, particularly as the critical Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint for regional tensions.

cards.headline: House passes pro-union bill with 20 Republican votes
cards.teaser: The Faster Labor Contracts Act passed the House after seven moderate Republicans joined Democrats to bring it to a vote over GOP leadership objections.
cards.body:
The House approved the Faster Labor Contracts Act on Tuesday, legislation designed to accelerate first-contract negotiations for newly unionized workers. The bill allows government intervention if negotiations stall beyond 90 days.

Twenty Republicans voted for the measure, supporting a significant priority for labor groups and populist lawmakers. The bill now advances toward the President for consideration.

cards.headline: Sen. Lindsey Graham wins South Carolina GOP primary
cards.teaser: Sen. Lindsey Graham won the South Carolina Republican Senate primary outright, avoiding a runoff in a crowded field.
cards.body:
Sen. Lindsey Graham won South Carolina's GOP Senate primary and will avoid a runoff, according to Decision Desk HQ projections. The four-term senator defeated Republican challenger Mark Lynch in a crowded field of candidates.

Graham's victory comes after President Trump endorsed him and participated in a tele-rally with the senator on Monday evening. Graham's win secures his position as the Republican nominee for the general election.

cards.headline: South Carolina GOP governor's race heads to runoff
cards.teaser: Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and state Attorney General Alan Wilson will face each other in a runoff for the Republican gubernatorial nomination.
cards.body:
The South Carolina GOP gubernatorial primary is headed to a runoff between Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and state Attorney General Alan Wilson, according to Decision Desk HQ projections. Neither candidate secured a majority of votes needed to win the nomination outright.

Evette has President Trump's endorsement in the race. The two Republicans were the top vote-getters in a field that included multiple candidates competing for the party's nomination.

cards.headline: Former Navy admiral advances to runoff in South Carolina Democratic primary
cards.teaser: Nancy Lacore, a three-star admiral fired by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, will face veteran Mac Deford in a runoff for the Democratic nomination.
cards.body:
Nancy Lacore, a three-star admiral fired by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last year, is projected to advance to a runoff in the Democratic primary for South Carolina's 1st Congressional District, according to Decision Desk HQ. She will face veteran Mac Deford in the runoff.

Lacore and Deford were the top two vote-getters among a field of Democratic candidates. The district stretches along the southeast coast of South Carolina.
